_note: Independent examples for a hold's entry and leg, from the AIM and the Instrument Flying Handbook (fetched from faa.gov on 2026-11-21), never from the code. Neither gives a worked entry with courses, so the entry cases read the AIM's own figure. Shape and checks as reference/atmosphere.json says.

cases.name: Sector (a): the parallel entry drawn from the northwest
cases.source: AIM (current edition, faa.gov aim_html, read 2026-11-21) 5-3-8 j.3, FIG 5-3-4 (Holding Pattern Entry Procedures), standard pattern, no wind: "Parallel Procedure. When approaching the holding fix from anywhere in sector (a) ... Teardrop Procedure ... sector (b) ... Direct Entry Procedure ... sector (c)". The figure draws the fix with the inbound leg along the page from right to left and the pattern above it; read with north up, the inbound course is 270 and the 70 degree line runs 020-200 through the fix.
cases.method: The dashed entry track drawn in sector (a) comes from about 315 degrees off the fix, a course of about 135 to it. The figure names no courses: the case reads its drawing with north up, and the entry depends only on the courses' difference. Tracks well inside a sector, never near its edge, where AIM 5-3-8 j.8(d) allows either entry within 5 degrees.

cases.name: The inbound leg at 14,000 ft MSL: 1 minute
cases.source: AIM (current edition, faa.gov aim_html, read 2026-11-21) 5-3-8 j.4(a), Timing, Inbound Leg: "At or below 14,000 feet MSL: 1 minute. Above 14,000 feet MSL: 1 1/2 minutes." Also FAA-H-8083-15B (Instrument Flying Handbook), ch. 10, p. 10-12, "Time Factors".
cases.method: Exact, the boundary from both sides.
